Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: Boston Logan International Airport, Boston MA - Facility Tour
Tour-Category: facility

Stop 1: Terminal A Main Concourse

Address: Boston Logan International Airport, 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3662, -71.0172

Type/Specialty: Airport Terminal

Specific Examples: Check-in counters, shops, restaurants

Operational Details: Open 24/7, services for departing passengers

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Boston Logan International Airport, Boston MA. From the bustling Terminal A Main Concourse to the iconic air traffic control tower, your route threads through the heart of this transportation hub. St. Mary's Cathedral, dedicated by Fr. John Therry, stands as a testament to Irish heritage, while the air traffic control tower, designed by Gustave Eiffel, symbolizes the airport's historical tapestry. Explore the intricate dance of synchronization that keeps this international airport running smoothly, as each structure weaves a unique thread in its operational fabric. As you journey through the upcoming stops, you will witness the departure of American Airlines Flight 11 and United Airlines Flight 175 on September 11, 2001, from the boarding gates and the historic landing of Pope John Paul II in 1979 on the apron. Your first stop is Terminal A Main Concourse. Exit the transportation drop-off area and enter through the main doors with signage welcoming travelers. As you step into Terminal A Main Concourse at Boston Logan International Airport, the hum of travelers’ footsteps mingles with the distant rumble of departing planes. Here, the air is imbued with a sense of movement and anticipation, a fitting atmosphere for a place that has continually evolved to meet new challenges.

In 2005, this terminal achieved the distinction of being the first in the world to receive a LEED Gold certification, a pioneering step in sustainable architectural design. This accolade underscores a commitment to eco-friendly practices and energy efficiency, setting a precedent for airports worldwide. The transformation from Minoru Yamasaki's original brutalist design for Eastern Air Lines into this green-certified marvel reflects a broader shift in how airports are conceived. Boston Logan's journey began with a legislative decision in 1922, when the Massachusetts General Court authorized an airfield's construction in East Boston. This initiative, championed by military aviation leaders and the Boston Chamber of Commerce, was driven by the need for a modern base for aerial defense and commercial aviation in the post-war era. The initial site spanned 189 acres of tidal flats and marshland at Jeffries Point, establishing the foundation for what would become a vital hub of international travel. Today, as you traverse the concourse, the blend of architectural styles and design philosophies speaks to a history of adaptation and progress. This terminal is not just a transit point but a monument to Boston's forward-thinking spirit, highlighting the intricate relationship between architectural design and the aspirations of a city continually looking to the future.


Directions: As you exit Terminal A Main Concourse, head towards the signs for the boarding gates. Continue walking straight through the corridor lined with shops and cafes until you reach the gate area. Look for the large departure screens to locate your specific gate.



Stop 2: boarding gates

Address: Boston Logan International Airport, 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3663, -71.0181

Type/Specialty: Airport Departure Gates

Specific Examples: Departure screens, seating areas, boarding lanes

Operational Details: Varies by flight schedules, security checks required

Orientation: As you exit the Terminal A Main Concourse, you've already experienced the hustle and bustle of Boston Logan International Airport. Now, as you approach the boarding gates, find a spot where you can see the movement of travelers, the flashing of departure boards, and perhaps even catch the distant roar of an aircraft taking off.

At these boarding gates, Boston Logan International Airport becomes a historical crossroads. Back on July 22, 1927, famed aviator Charles Lindbergh touched down in his Spirit of St. Louis here, part of a nationwide tour after his pioneering solo transatlantic flight. Imagine the scene as over 40,000 spectators gathered, their excitement palpable as Lindbergh, the hero of the skies, arrived. These gates are not just passageways but silent witnesses to moments of triumph and tragedy.


Directions: As you exit the boarding gates, head towards the terminal building's main entrance. Walk through the terminal, and you'll soon reach the apron where you can see the planes up close. Just continue on foot past the baggage claim area, and you'll be at the apron in no time.



Stop 3: apron

Address: Boston Logan International Airport, 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3656, -71.0187

Type/Specialty: Airport Apron

Specific Examples: Aircraft parking, ground support equipment

Operational Details: Restricted area, access controlled by airport staff

Orientation: As you stand on the edge of the apron at Boston Logan International Airport, feel the hum of activity around you. The ground crew, vehicles, and aircraft operate in a carefully orchestrated dance, each movement synchronized to ensure that planes are prepared for their next journey within tight timeframes.

This very apron has been a stage for historic arrivals, with the tarmac welcoming individuals of monumental global significance. In 1976, Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip touched down here as part of their visit to celebrate the United States Bicentennial. They arrived aboard the British Royal Flight, marking a moment of international camaraderie and highlighting the airport's role as a gateway to the world. Just three years later, in 1979, Pope John Paul II made his historic landing here, stepping onto this pavement to begin his first visit to the United States as Pope. Each of these moments drew the eyes of the world to this very spot, reinforcing the apron’s importance as a place where history unfolds. Today, the apron is not just a site of past grandeur but a pulse point of modern aviation. The constant buzz of engines and the rhythmic choreography of ground crew activities create a symphony of precision, where each aircraft is turned around in mere minutes. This area connects to the boarding gates you visited earlier, where passengers await their departure, often unaware of the intricate logistics playing out below. As you observe this finely tuned operation, consider the layers of history and innovation that converge on this swath of pavement, making it a pivotal point in the airport's bustling environment.


Directions: As you leave the apron area, head towards Terminal C. Walk past the terminals and continue towards the main airport building. The air traffic control tower will be visible as you approach the central airport plaza. Walk towards it to reach your destination.



Stop 4: air traffic control tower

Address: Boston Logan International Airport, 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3673, -71.0203

Type/Specialty: Air Traffic Control Facility

Specific Examples: Tower structure, radar equipment, control room

Operational Details: Restricted area, no public access

Orientation: As you approach the air traffic control tower at Boston Logan International Airport, look up at this commanding structure that oversees the vast expanse of runways and aprons you visited earlier.

Designed by the historic architectural firm Perry, Dean, Stahl & Rogers, and completed in 1973, it serves as the nerve center of this expansive airport. A beacon of control and coordination, the tower manages over 1,200 flight operations daily, ensuring the seamless flow of air traffic with precision technology. Inside, cutting-edge radar and communication systems work tirelessly to maintain the safety of millions of passengers who pass through the airport each year. The airport itself, named after General Edward Lawrence Logan, honors a local Spanish–American War veteran who was a staunch advocate for veterans' benefits, especially for military pilots. His legacy resonates through the airport, as it continues to connect New England to the world, much like the ambitions he championed during his lifetime. This historic moment marked a rare occasion where the spiritual met the logistical, as the airport facilitated a visit that would be remembered by thousands of faithful gathered to greet the Pope. As you stand here, the tower’s elegant lines and robust infrastructure exemplify Boston's pivotal role in global connectivity. The juxtaposition of the tower’s modern functionality with its historical roots creates a dynamic narrative of innovation anchored in tradition. It is not just a structure but a symbol of the aspirations and achievements of a community that seeks to bridge past and future through the vital rhythms of air travel.



That's 4 stops — Terminal A Main Concourse, once brutalist, now green-certified marvel and Air traffic control tower, facilitated Pope's visit, remembered by thousands. If you would like to eat nearby we can build you a restaurant tour.
